settings.title: Settings
settings.smart_switch_hint: Move the earbuds to whichever device starts playing
settings.notif_mirror_hint: Show the phone's notifications on this laptop
settings.notif_send_hint: Show this laptop's notifications on the phone
settings.proximity_lock_hint: Lock this laptop when your phone goes out of Bluetooth range (only while you're idle)
settings.proximity_unlock_hint: When your phone comes back, the laptop unlocks by itself (re-locks if untouched for 90s)
settings.clipboard_sync_hint: Text copied on either device appears on the other. Phone→laptop needs the phone's Quick Settings tile.
settings.file_auto_accept_hint: Save files shared from your phone without asking. Only your paired phone can send them.
settings.uc_hint: Glide the laptop cursor & keyboard onto the phone. Push the screen edge to cross; push back to return.
settings.uc_needs: Needs USB debugging (adb) and Wayland — the screen edge is held through the compositor's input-capture portal. Tested on GNOME 45+; KDE Plasma 6.1+ and Hyprland ship that portal too but are untested here, Sway does not have it, and X11 has no such thing. Two-finger scrolling is drawn as a real finger, which only phones that let adb write /dev/uinput allow — elsewhere it falls back to wheel steps. Hiding the laptop's own cursor is GNOME-only, and needs one log-out after installing.
settings.uc_err_no_injector: No injector — the native cursor needs adb. Turn on USB debugging and allow it on the phone.
settings.uc_err_no_display_size: Could not read the phone's screen size over adb. Check that the phone still shows as a device.
settings.uc_err_no_portal: This desktop does not offer the input-capture portal, so the cursor cannot be held at the screen edge. It needs Wayland — GNOME 45+, KDE Plasma 6.1+ or Hyprland.
settings.uc_err_session_refused: The desktop refused an input-capture session.
settings.uc_err_no_zones: The desktop reported no screen areas to arm. Reconnecting a monitor usually fixes it.
settings.uc_err_barrier_refused: The compositor would not arm that edge — something else already holds it. Try a corner instead of the whole edge.

settings.footer: End-to-end encrypted over your own link

intro.welcome_sub: Choose your language to get started.
intro.whatis_title: Your phone and laptop, as one.
intro.whatis_body: Private. Local. No cloud — everything stays on your devices.

feat.earbuds_body: Press play on your laptop and your Bluetooth earbuds hand off from the phone — automatically.
feat.phone_body: Notifications, calls, SMS and contacts — mirrored and answerable right from the desktop.
feat.clipboard_body: Copy here, paste there. Your notes and todos stay in sync across both devices.
feat.mirror_body: See your phone on your laptop and control it with your mouse and keyboard — it even works as a webcam.
feat.handoff_body: Reading a link on your phone? Open the same page on your laptop in one tap.
feat.files_body: Share photos, documents and anything else between your phone and laptop — they land in Downloads.
feat.proximity_body: Your laptop locks itself when your phone walks away — and unlocks the moment you're back.

intro.privacy_body: End-to-end encrypted over your own Bluetooth & Wi-Fi link. No servers, no accounts, nothing in the cloud.
intro.ready_body: Let's link your phone — it only takes a moment.
intro.ble_tip_title: One thing for a rock-solid link
intro.ble_tip_body: Close other phone-link apps that use Bluetooth, like KDE Connect. They hold the same Bluetooth LE radio and can block Vortex from connecting.
